dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Extremal Graph Theory
dossier_meta.statement_text: An $ H $ -factor in a graph $ G $ is a set of vertex-disjoint copies of $ H $ covering all vertices of $ G $ . Problem Let $ c $ be a fixed positive real number and $ H $ a fixed graph. Is it NP-hard to determine whether a graph $ G $ on $ n $ vertices and minimum degree $ cn $ contains and $ H $ -factor?
dossier_meta.context_text: The answer is positive for cliques and a few other graphs [KO06]. If we remove the minimum degree condition, the problem is NP-complete if and only if $ H $ has a component which contains at least 3 vertices, as shown by Hell and Kirkpatrick [HK].
dossier_meta.references_text:
- [HK] P. Hell and D.G. Kirkpatrick, On the complexity of general graph factor problems, SIAM J. Computing 12 (1983), 601-609.
- [KO06] D. Kühn and D. Osthus, Critical chromatic number and the complexity of perfect packings in graphs, Proceedings of the 17th ACM-SIAM Symposium on Discrete Algorithms (SODA), 2006.
- *[KO09] D. Kühn and D. Osthus, The minimum degree threshold for perfect graph packings, Combinatorica 29 (2009), 65-107.
